source: Editorial Willow feed. Ratings are cited from public reviews, not a live IMDb scrape.

items.title: The Shawshank Redemption
items.summary: Banker Andy Dufresne, wrongly imprisoned, keeps hope and friendship with Red while quietly planning escape.
items.whyToWatch: Timeless prison drama about resilience and hope — still the most cited “greatest film” on IMDb.

items.title: The Godfather
items.summary: The Corleone family’s rise in organized crime, told through Michael’s reluctant turn from outsider to don.
items.whyToWatch: Iconic crime saga — a masterclass in storytelling and acting, still treated as one of cinema’s peaks.

items.title: The Dark Knight
items.summary: Batman faces the Joker’s chaos in Gotham, and the city’s idea of justice starts to crack.
items.whyToWatch: Superhero filmmaking at its sharpest — Heath Ledger’s Joker is still the performance people measure others against.

items.title: Everything Everywhere All at Once
items.summary: An exhausted immigrant laundromat owner discovers she can jump universes — and has to hold her family together while she does.
items.whyToWatch: Inventive, funny, and sincerely emotional sci-fi. Oscar-winning, and it earns the weirdness.

items.title: Inception
items.summary: A thief who steals secrets from dreams is hired to plant an idea instead — and can no longer trust what is real.
items.whyToWatch: Mind-bending thriller with layered set pieces. Christopher Nolan at full craft.

items.title: Breaking Bad
items.summary: Chemistry teacher Walter White starts cooking meth after a diagnosis, and the quiet man becomes someone else.
items.whyToWatch: The character study people still call one of the greatest TV dramas ever made.

items.title: Band of Brothers
items.summary: Easy Company from training through the European theater — friendship first, then the cost of the war.
items.whyToWatch: Spielberg and Hanks’ war miniseries: careful, heavy, and unusually exact about the unit’s real path.

items.title: Chernobyl
items.summary: The 1986 nuclear disaster, the people who contained it, and the lies that made it worse.
items.whyToWatch: A short, haunting miniseries praised for how plainly it shows the human cost.

items.title: Peaky Blinders
items.summary: Tommy Shelby’s Birmingham gang climbs from post-WWI street power into politics and empire.
items.whyToWatch: Stylish crime drama with a cultural afterlife — clothes, score, and Cillian Murphy’s stare.

items.title: Stranger Things
items.summary: Kids in 1980s Indiana stumble into a government lab, a missing friend, and something from the Upside Down.
items.whyToWatch: Nostalgic sci-fi adventure that mixes friendship, horror, and pop-culture comfort — the family-night series.
